title: Gravitation
seo_title: Gravitation Class 11 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 7)
standard_text: Kepler's laws of planetary motion, universal law of gravitation, acceleration due to gravity and its variation with altitude and depth, gravitational potential energy and gravitational potential, escape speed, orbital velocity of a satellite.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 7 Gravitation: Kepler's laws, Newton's law of gravitation, g with height and depth, potential energy, orbital and escape speed. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Escape speed √(2gR); orbital speed √(gR) near the surface.
body_html:
How to think about it

Kepler found that planets move in ellipses, sweep equal areas in equal times and have T² ∝ r³. Newton's law F = Gm₁m₂/r² explains them, with G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². At the surface g = GM/R² = 9.8 m/s²; it falls with height, g/(1 + h/R)², and with depth, g(1 − d/R).

Gravitational potential energy is −GMm/r. A body must reach the escape speed √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s to leave the Earth, while a satellite close to the surface needs √(gR) ≈ 7.9 km/s. Geostationary satellites orbit once in 24 hours.

Example

g at height R?

9.8/2²

Answer: 2.45 m/s²

Example

Orbit 4 times Earth's radius. Period?

4^(3/2)

Answer: 8 years

Common mistakes

  • Thinking there is no gravity on astronauts in orbit.
  • Using g(1 − d/R) for height.
  • Thinking escape speed depends on the body's mass.
